==English==
{{swp|<dab!>}}
[[File:Gordijnen aan venster.JPG|thumb|A '''window''', viewed from inside.]]

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂weh₁-|*h₃ekʷ-}}
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:wyndowe|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|wyndowe}}, {{m|enm|wyndown}}, from {{der|en|non|vindauga|t=window|lit=wind-eye; wind-hole}}, equivalent to {{com|en|wind|eye|nocat=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|windae}} and {{m|sco|windock}}, {{cog|fo|vindeyga}}, {{cog|nb|vindu}}, {{cog|nn|vindauge}}, {{cog|da|vindue}}, archaic {{cog|sv|vindöga}}, {{cog|ovd|windog}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ēagþȳrel|lit=eye hole}} (the rare direct descendant is {{m|en|eyethurl||window, pupil, etc.}}). The “windows” among early Germanic peoples were just unglazed holes (eyes) in the wall or roof that permitted wind to pass through {{rfv-etym|en}}.

For semantic parallels, compare {{cog|got|𐌰𐌿𐌲𐌰𐌳𐌰𐌿𐍂𐍉|t=window|lit=eye-door}}; {{cog|la-vul|*ventāna}}, from {{m|la|ventus||wind}}; and {{cog|sla-pro|*okъnò||window}}, from {{m|sla-pro|*ȍko||eye}}.

===Noun===
{{wp|,+ (computing)}}
{{en-noun|~}}

# An opening, usually covered by one or more panes of clear glass, to allow light and air from outside to enter a building or vehicle.
#: {{ux|en| She opened the '''window''' to let some air in.}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=1|passage=But then I had the [massive] flintlock by me for protection. ¶{{...}}The linen-press and a chest on the top of it formed, however, a very good gun-carriage; and, thus mounted, aim could be taken out of the '''window''' at the old mare feeding in the meadow below by the brook, and a 'bead' could be drawn upon Molly, the dairymaid, kissing the fogger behind the hedge,{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1952|author=w:L. F. Salzman|title=Building in England|page=173
|passage=A '''window''' is an opening in a wall to admit light and air.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=14|passage=Nanny Broome was looking up at the outer wall.  Just under the ceiling there were three lunette '''windows''', heavily barred and blacked out in the normal way by centuries of grime.}}
# An opening, usually covered by glass, in a shop which allows people to view the shop and its products from outside; a [[shop window]].
#* {{RQ:Birmingham Gossamer|chapter=I|passage=There is an hour or two, after the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.{{...}}Passengers wander restlessly about or hurry, with futile energy, from place to place. Pushing men hustle each other at the '''windows''' of the purser's office, under pretence of expecting letters or despatching telegrams.}}
# {{lb|en|architecture|nocat=1}} The [[shutter]], [[casement]], [[sash]] with its fittings, or other [[framework]], which closes a window opening.
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A period of time when something is available or possible; a limited [[opportunity]].
#: {{co|en|launch '''window'''}}
#: {{co|en|'''window''' of opportunity}}
#: {{ux|en|You have a two-hour '''window''' of clear weather to finish working on the lawn.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Euan McKirdy; Hilary Whiteman|title=Thai cave rescue: Divers enter cave to free boys|url=https://edition.cnn.com/asia/live-news/thai-cave-rescue-live-intl/index.html|date=2018-07-08|accessdate=2018-07-08|passage=But rescuers have a dwindling '''window''' of opportunity, with forecasters predicting the return of heavy monsoon rains in the coming days, effectively sealing off the cave until October.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Euan McKirdy; et al.|title=Arrest warrant to be issued for former Thai PM Yingluck Shinawatra|date=2017-08-25|accessdate=2017-08-25|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2017/08/24/asia/yingluck-shinawatra-trial-verdict/index.html|passage=Now she'll be thinking about fleeing. (The verdict delay) provides a '''window''' for potential flight....if she has not fled already.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Luke Harding|quotee={{w|Institute for the Study of War}}|title=Russian forces make significant gains in eastern Ukraine|date=2024-04-23|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/23/russian-forces-make-significant-gains-in-eastern-ukraine|author2=Dan Sabbagh|passage=“The Russian military command is likely aware of the closing window before more western aid arrives and is trying to secure offensive gains before the '''window''' closes,” it said in a briefing on Monday.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011111321/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/23/russian-forces-make-significant-gains-in-eastern-ukraine|archivedate=11 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Something that allows one to see through or into something.
#: {{ux|en|His journal provides a rare '''window''' into his otherwise obscure life.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=The Baltic: Arena of Power|author=Priit J. Vesilind|page=604
|text=Leningrad, Russia's traditional '''window''' on the West, finds the world peering back in fascination.}}
# A restricted range.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Patrick R. Nicolas|title=Scala for Machine Learning|page=109
|passage=In this case, a band-pass filter using a range or '''window''' of frequencies is appropriate to isolate the frequency or the group of frequencies that characterize a specific cycle.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q835016}} {{lb|en|graphical user interface}} A rectangular area on a computer [[terminal]] or screen containing some kind of [[user interface]], displaying [[output]] and allowing [[input]], often for a single task in a [[multitasking]] system.
# A [[figure]] formed of [[line]]s [[cross]]ing each other.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1709|author={{w|William King (poet)|William King}}|title=Art of Cookery
|passage=till he has '''windows''' on his bread and butter}}
# {{lb|en|medicine}} The time between first infection and detectability.
# {{lb|en|military|historical|uncountable}} {{synonym of|en|chaff||strips of material intended to confuse radar}} <!--this was the British code name-->
# {{lb|en|signal processing}} A function multiplied with a signal to reduce spectral leakage when performing a Fourier transform.
# {{lb|en|geology}} A [[fenster]]: a geologic or [[tectonic window]]. 
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1927|author=Léon William Collet|title=The Structure of the Alps|page=232
|text={{...}}the Hohe Tauern '''window'''. In the transverse depression between the '''windows''', the Silvretta Nappe disappears almost entirely underneath the Oetztal Nappe. The southern margin of the Northern Limestone zone is formed by the "Greywacke zone" of{{nb...}}}}
